ai.seo_question: How does the silence of the ignorant person serve as a description of their nature?
ai.summary: Sharif al-Raḍī defines ignorance not merely as a lack of knowledge, but as a fundamental misplacement of attributes, where the ignorant person fails to distinguish essence from accident. This error renders their silence or absence of description a defining characteristic in itself, serving as a stark antithesis to the precise discernment of the wise. This commentary highlights the epistemological rigor central to Shia wisdom literature, emphasizing that true understanding requires correct ontological categorization.

en.sayed-ali-raza: The meaning is that the ignorant is one who does not place things in their proper positions. In this way, Amīr al-mu’minīn’s abstention from describing was a way of describing him because his attributes are just the opposite of the wise.
